entities.name: Dry Tree
entities.summary: Monstrous leafless tree, about a hundred feet tall with some fifty great limbs, hung with knights' arms of many unknown blazons; its roots in a poisoned, mirror-still pool; perhaps made, perhaps grown.

refs.q: rose up a huge and monstrous tree, whose topmost branches were even the horns which they had seen from below the hill's brow

entities.name: (unnamed) valley of the Dry Tree
entities.summary: Theatre-like valley ringed by the ridge, open by one narrow pass, its stepped slopes lined with the dead.

refs.q: the said valley was like to one of those theatres of the ancient Roman Folk

entities.name: (unnamed) poison pool of the Dry Tree
entities.summary: Clear pool round the tree's roots that does not ripple in the wind; a crow dies after drinking.

refs.q: when the wind eddies about, and lifts the skirts of our raiment, it makes no ripple on the face of the pool, and doubtless it is heavy with venom

spatial.terrain_text: on a mound or islet in a pool at the centre

refs.q: a very midmost of this dreary theatre rose up a huge and monstrous tree

spatial.terrain_text: ringed by a great ridge, with a narrow pass on the further side

refs.q: about which on all sides went the ridge, save where it was broken down into a narrow pass on the further side

facts.subject: (unnamed) poison pool of the Dry Tree
facts.statement: The pool is poisonous; a crow that drinks dies at once.

refs.q: ere he was many feet off the ground he gave a grievous croak, and turning over in the air fell down stark dead

facts.subject: Dry Tree
facts.statement: The tree seems to have growth in it: its roots spread and waver in the water.

refs.q: it seemed to them as though the Tree had verily growth in it

facts.subject: (unnamed) valley of the Dry Tree
facts.statement: The dead all wear the same grin, "as though they had died in pain, and yet beguiled".

refs.q: each of the dead leathery faces was drawn up in a grin as though they had died in pain, and yet beguiled

facts.subject: Ralph
facts.statement: After nearly drinking, Ralph is entranced, collapses, and forgets the danger; Ursula's ruse saves him.

refs.q: Shall we not go down into the valley?  there is naught there to harm us

facts.subject: Thirsty Desert
facts.statement: No way-token is near the pool, unlike at other watering-places.

refs.q: there is no sign of the way hereabout, as at other watering-steads

facts.subject: Dry Tree
facts.statement: The tree is hung with blazoned shields, helms, swords, spears, axes and hauberks of many unknown fashions.

refs.q: The limbs of that tree were all behung with blazoned shields and knight's helms, and swords, and spears, and axes, and hawberks

events.label: At the Dry Tree
events.summary: The lovers find the Dry Tree; Ursula prevents Ralph drinking the poisoned pool and lures him away.

refs.q: then from both their lips at once came the cry THE DRY TREE

unresolved.question: Whether the Dry Tree is made by hands or grown.

refs.q: they doubted whether it were not made by men's hands rather than grown up out of the earth

unresolved.question: The Dry Tree here is a deathtrap, while the Swevenham tale said touching its bole would lead to the Well (BTWO-C16).

refs.q: doubtless it is heavy with venom

opportunities.idea: A landmark trap (the poisoned pool) with environmental warnings (no ripple, no waymark) that perceptive players can read.

basis_refs.q: it makes no ripple on the face of the pool

opportunities.idea: The real Dry Tree versus imitations (Utterbol's worshipped tree, Hampton's fellowship name).

ledger.summary: Over a great ridge they see horn-like branches: a valley like a Roman theatre, ringed by the ridge except for a narrow pass on the far side, its slopes lined with dead men and women, many with drawn swords, all grinning as if beguiled in pain. In the middle stands a monstrous leafless tree about a hundred feet high with some fifty great limbs hung with shields, helms, swords, spears, axes and hauberks of unknown blazons, its roots in a mirror-still pool. Both cry "The Dry Tree". Ralph kneels to drink; Ursula sees the water does not ripple in the wind and stops him; a crow drinks and falls dead. Ralph is entranced; Ursula lures him up the slope by crying that their horses are threatened, then revives him with water and cordial. They ride away.
ledger.geography_notes: In the Thirsty Desert, a great ridge encloses a bowl-shaped valley like an ancient theatre, open only by a narrow pass on the far side. At its centre the Dry Tree stands on a mound or islet in a clear, still, poisonous pool. The slopes are stepped.
open_questions: Is the Dry Tree made or grown? (the text wavers)
